en.headline: Bar Association backs criminalising bid-rigging and proposes about 50 law changes
en.dek: The Hong Kong Bar Association's Tai Po fire task force report, released on Sunday, supports a dual civil-criminal track under the Competition Ordinance while urging clear definitions, and suggests dual-envelope tenders for larger owners' corporation works.
body: The Hong Kong Bar Association said on Sunday that it supports in principle amending the Competition Ordinance to criminalise bid-rigging, running alongside the existing civil enforcement regime, as part of roughly 50 proposed legislative changes across at least six ordinances.

Its Tai Po fire legal research task force, which began work in January and published its report on Sunday, stressed that the elements of any new criminal offence — including the definition of bid-rigging, the burden of proof and the required mental element — must be clearly defined. The association noted that civil and criminal proceedings would not proceed simultaneously for the same case, to avoid double jeopardy, and that enforcement agencies would need to coordinate on the appropriate track.

Among other recommendations, the report proposes amending the Building Management Ordinance so that owners' corporation projects above a specified value use a dual-envelope system: a technical proposal that must meet a published minimum score before the price envelope is opened. Assessment criteria and weightings would have to be disclosed to all owners. Additional suggestions cover safety-record disclosures, conflict-of-interest declarations for professionals, and stronger fire-safety responsibilities for property managers under related ordinances.

The association said the work was independent and aimed at improving transparency in tender assessment, breaking conflict chains and deterring anti-competitive conduct in building maintenance. The government has already indicated it plans to introduce criminal offences for certain anti-competitive conduct in building maintenance tenders as part of wider reforms following the Wang Fuk Court fire.

zh.headline: 大律師公會支持圍標刑事化 提約50項修例建議
zh.dek: 大律師公會大埔火災法律研究小組周日發表報告，原則支持修訂《競爭條例》將圍標刑事化，並與現行民事執法雙軌並行，同時促請罪行元素定義清晰，並建議法團大型工程採雙信封投標。
body: 香港大律師公會周日表示，原則支持修訂《競爭條例》將圍標行為刑事化，與現行民事執法制度雙軌並行，這是公會就至少六條法例提出約50項修訂建議的一部分。
公會今年1月成立的大埔火災法律研究小組周日發表報告。公會強調，新刑事罪行的元素，包括圍標定義、舉證責任及犯罪意圖等，必須清晰。公會指出，民事與刑事程序不會就同一案件同時進行，以避免違反一罪不二審原則，執法機關需協調決定採取哪一軌道。
報告其他建議包括，修訂《建築物管理條例》，規定業主立案法團工程超過指定金額時，標書須以雙信封形式遞交：技術建議書必須先達到評估指定最低分數，方可開啟價格建議書。評估基準及比重須向全體業主公佈。其他建議涵蓋安全紀錄披露、專業人士利益申報，以及加強物業管理公司在消防安全方面的法定責任等。
公會表示，工作獨立進行，目標是確保招標評審過程透明、切斷利益鏈，以及遏止樓宇維修方面的反競爭行為。政府早前已表示，將就樓宇維修招標中的嚴重反競爭行為引入刑事罪行，作為宏福苑火災後更廣泛改革的一部分。
